translations.text: Discourse of our holy and blessed father Basil, archbishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, on holy baptism, addressed to those
who were receiving baptism late; for the custom at that time was that people be baptized at thirty years of age, but some were not baptized until forty or sixty years of age.
But we, who received holy baptism in infancy and afterward defiled it with our sin, let us now understand this as a call to repentance.
The wise Solomon, when he was dividing the times for the affairs of this world and appointing for each affair its own time, spoke thus:
"There is a time for every matter: there is a time of birth and there is a time of death."
But I, who am preaching to you this preaching of life, will change that saying of the wise man slightly and say:
"There is a time of death and there is a time of birth." And what is the reason for this change?

For he was speaking of those who are born and perish, and therefore, in keeping with the nature of the flesh, he mentioned birth before death, for it is impossible for one who has not first been born to taste death.
But I, who intend to speak about spiritual birth, set death before life,
For through the death of the flesh the birth of the spirit is given to us, as the Lord says:
"I kill and I make alive." Let us die, then, O brothers, so that we may be made alive.
Let us put to death the mind and the thinking of the flesh, which cannot submit to the law of God,
so that the mind and the thought of the spirit may become strong in us, from which life and peace come to us.
Let us be buried with Christ, who died for us, so that we may rise with him who has graciously granted us resurrection.
For the time for other affairs is a suitable season: a time of sleep and a time of wakefulness, a time of war and a time of peace; but the time of baptism is the whole of human life.
For neither is life of the body possible without breathing, nor is life possible for the soul that does not know its Creator, for ignorance of God is the death of the soul.
And whoever has not received baptism is not enlightened; and without light neither can the eye see what belongs to it, nor does the soul have the power to receive the knowledge of God.
For every time is good for baptism and for life: whether you say night or day, or an hour, or a grain of an hour, or something smaller still.
But the fitness of its own proper day is exceedingly good. And again, what could be closer to baptism than that day of fullness [?]?
For that day is the memorial of the resurrection, and baptism is a power toward resurrection.
On the day of the resurrection, then, let us receive the grace of the resurrection.
For this reason the Church calls her children from afar with a lofty proclamation, so that those whom she earlier conceived in the womb
she may then give birth to, and suckle them with the words of teaching, and feed them the solid food of faith.
John preached the baptism of repentance, and all Judea went out to him.
The Lord preaches the baptism of adoption as sons, and who among those who trust in him will not listen?
That baptism was an introduction to repentance, but this one brings to perfection; that one was a separation from sin, but this one is kinship with God.
That preaching was of one man, John, and he drew everyone to repentance; but you are taught by the prophets, who say:
"Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean"; from the Psalms you hear: "Come to the Lord and receive light"; from the apostles the good news is brought to you:
"Repent and be baptized, each one of you, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the promise of the Holy Spirit";
and you are taught by the Lord himself, who says: "Come to me, all who are weary and heavy laden, and I will give you rest."
For all this has come together today in the reading, and do you shrink in dread, and are you negligent, and do you go on deliberating?
From childhood you have heard the truth, and have you still not come to the truth? You are always being taught, and have you still not come to understanding?
You are a tester all your days, a spy [?] until old age; when will you ever become a Christian? When will we know you as one of ours?
Last year you were waiting for this year, and now are you again waiting for the coming one? Take care that you are not found to be one who promises himself many seasons.
You do not know what tomorrow will be. Do not make a promise of what is not yours.
We are calling you to life, man; why do you flee from this calling? We are summoning you to what is good; why do you pass by the gift?
The kingdom of heaven stands open, the one who calls does not deceive, the road is easy to travel.
Neither time, nor expense, nor trading is needed; why are you negligent? Why do you flee?
Why are you afraid of the yoke, like an untried heifer? "It is sweet, it is light"; it does not wound the neck but brings it honor.
For its strap is not tied on the throat; rather, it seeks one who will bear it of his own free will.
Do you not see that Ephraim is reproached like a bull gone wild, because he strayed lawlessly and held the yoke of the law in contempt?
Bend that untamed neck of yours, become a beast of burden [?] for Christ, so that you may not be loose from the straps and straying in the world and easily carried off by wild beasts.
"Taste and see that the Lord is sweet." How could I describe the sweetness of honey to those who do not know it?
Taste and see for yourselves in this tasting, for it is able to convince more than any word.
The Jew does not put off circumcision, because of the word that says:
"Every soul that is not circumcised on the eighth day shall be cut off from its people."
But you flee from the circumcision made without hands, which is accomplished through baptism by the stripping off of the flesh, you who have heard from the Lord himself:
"Amen, amen, I say to you, unless a person is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of heaven,"
and there, there is pain and a wound, but here the dew of the Spirit and the healing of the wounds of the heart.
Do you worship the one who died for you? Then accept burial with him through baptism.
If you are not conformed to the likeness of his death, how will you become a partaker of his resurrection?
Israel was baptized by Moses in the cloud and in the sea, for it was showing you a figure and depicting this truth that was to appear in the last times,
but you flee from baptism, which is not prefigured in a sea but is accomplished in truth:
not by a cloud but by the Spirit, not by Moses the servant but by Christ the Creator.
If Israel had not crossed the sea, it would not have been released from the slavery of Pharaoh; and you, if you do not pass through that water, will not be saved from the bitter tyranny of the devil.
Israel would not have drunk from that spiritual rock if it had not been baptized in figure; nor will anyone give you that true drink if you are not baptized in truth.
Israel ate the bread of angels after baptism, but how will you eat that bread of life if you do not first receive baptism?
Israel entered the land of promise because of baptism, but how will you return to paradise if you are not sealed by baptism?
Or do you not know that a sword of fire is appointed to guard the way to the tree, and that it is terrifying and burning to unbelievers, but shines sweetly and beautifully for believers?
And the King made it a turning sword, for when it sees a believer it turns its back, but if it sees one of the unbaptized it confronts him face to face.
Elijah was not afraid of the chariot of fire and the horses of fire that came to him,
but in his desire to ascend to heaven he dared those terrifying things and joyfully mounted those chariots of fire, he who was still in the flesh.
But you, who need to ascend not on chariots of fire but to be raised up to heaven by water and the Spirit, do you not hasten toward that calling?
Elijah showed the power of baptism on the altar of sacrifice, he who not with fire
but with water burned up the offering, although the nature of fire is ever at war with water.
Since, then, the water was at that time mystically poured three times upon the sacrifice, it became the beginning of the fire and kindled the flame as oil would, for he said:
"Bring a measure of water and pour it on the altar and on the wood." And he said, "Pour it a second time also, and a third time," and they poured it.
And that word showed that through baptism the baptized person draws near to God, and
that the holy and heavenly light shines forth in the soul of the baptized through faith in the Trinity.
If I were distributing gold to the people, you would not say, "I will come tomorrow, and you can give it to me tomorrow," but you would eagerly ask me for that money and be grieved over the delay.
But since the generous Giver sets before you not the color of a material thing but the purity of the soul,
you find excuses and enumerate your lack of leisure, when you ought to run toward that gift. O wonder!
You are renewed without being dissolved, purified without a furnace, born a second time without being crushed, healed without pain, and have you counted that grace as nothing?
If you were a slave of men and freedom for slaves were decreed in writing, would you not hasten to be set free?
And you would hire helpers and entreat judges, so that by that means you might attain freedom,
or you would even endure blows and wounds at that time, in order to escape beating thereafter.
Since, then, you are a slave not of men but of sin, and the herald calls you to freedom,
So that he may free you from captivity, make you a fellow citizen of the angels, and show you to be a son of God, adopted by grace and an heir of the good things of Christ, you say:
"It is not yet the time to receive what is given." O these wicked corruptions! O that defiled and endless busyness!
How long will there be desires? How long will there be tastes for filthy things?
We have spent much time in the service of the world; let us now spend a little for ourselves as well. What can be given in exchange for the soul?
What is equal in worth to the kingdom of heaven? Who is a more trustworthy counsellor for you than God?
Who is wiser than the Wise One? Or who is better than the Good One? Who is closer to you and more honorable than the Creator?
Eve gained nothing either, for she believed the counsel of the serpent rather than that of God. O those improper words of yours!
"I have no leisure," he says, "to be healed; do not show me the light, do not unite me to the King." Do you not speak in this way, and with words even more foolish than these?
But if you were written down under a great debt, and a remission of debts were proclaimed for debtors, and then there were someone
who was eager that the remission of debts not be given to you, would you not mourn and cry out that he was taking away from you the grace given to all?
Since, then, not only forgiveness of what is past but also gifts of good things to come are proclaimed, you harm your own self in such a way
as not one of your enemies could harm you, and you suppose that you are deliberating well and devising what is better for yourself, you who do not accept the remission
but die in those debts, you who know that the debtor of the ten thousand talents found forgiveness,
had he not himself renewed the judgment by his mercilessness toward his fellow. This is to be feared by us too, lest it come upon us
when we have received the grace, if we do not forgive our debtors, so that in this way the gift may be secure for us.
Enter into the treasury of your soul, and stir up the remembrance of your deeds.
If your sins are many, do not cut off hope because of their multitude, for:
"Where sin abounded, there grace abounded all the more," if you accept the grace.
For the one who owes much will also be forgiven much, so that he may love all the more.
But if your sins are small and slight and not deadly, why are you anxious about that later time,
you who did not spend the past improperly, even when you were not yet sealed?
Now understand it in this way: your soul stands as if on a scale, and on one side it is drawn by angels and on the other side toward demons.
To whom will you give the inclination of your heart? Who will prevail in you: the lust of the flesh or the holiness of the soul?
Passing pleasure, or desire for the good things that do not pass away? Will angels lead you away, or will those who have held you keep you in their grip?
In battle, commanders give a sign to those who follow them, so that friends may easily call to one another and, when they clash with their opponents, may be recognized.
But no one will be able to recognize whether you are ours or belong to the adversaries, unless you receive that good sign, unless the light of the Lord's face appears upon you.
How will the angel defend you, or how will he rescue you from enemies, if he does not recognize the seal?
Or how will you say, "I belong to God," when you do not have his sign?
Or do you not know that the destroyer passed by the marked houses, but in the unmarked ones he slew the firstborn?
An unsealed treasure is easy to steal; an unmarked sheep is carried off without effort.
Are you young? Keep your youth from going astray with the bridle of baptism. Has the youth of your years passed?
Do not be deprived of provisions for the journey, do not lose your guardian, do not think of the eleventh hour
as of the first, since even one who has just entered this life ought to keep its end before his eyes.
If some physician promised you that by some means he would turn you back from old age to youth, would you not long for the coming of the day when you would see yourself returned to youth?
Since, then, baptism has promised you the rejuvenation of your soul, which you have made old and corrupt and defiled by iniquities,
do you despise the benefactor and not hasten toward that promise?
Do you not desire to see what the great wonder of this matter is? How a person is born without a mother?
How what has grown old and been corrupted by the desires of deception is renewed again, becomes young, and comes to the true flower of youth?
Baptism is the redeemer of captives, the forgiveness of debts, the death of sin, the second birth of the soul,
a garment of light, an unbreakable seal, a chariot to heaven, the herald of the kingdom, the grace of adoption.
Than these so many and so great good things, O wretched one, the taste of sin seems more precious to you,
for I understand your thoughts, even if you do not speak them in words; the deeds themselves cry out, even if you are silent with your mouth.
"Leave me be, let me use my flesh for foul desires, let me wallow in the mire of sin, let me defile my hands with blood,
let me seize what belongs to others, let me walk in deceit, let me swear falsely, let me lie; and when at some time I cease from these evils, then I will receive baptism."
Now if sin is good, keep it until the end; but if it is harmful to the one who commits it, why do you linger in these evils?
Who is there who wishes to vomit up the bile gathered from harmful foods, and yet gathers it in still greater abundance?
For the body ought to be cleansed of those harmful things, not to accumulate them beyond its strength.
It is evident how far a ship can bear the weight of its cargo, and if more than the measure is loaded into it, it sinks.
You too should fear lest the same thing befall you, lest you commit sins beyond forgiveness and sink before entering the harbor.
Or does God not see those deeds of yours? Does he not know your thoughts? Or does he assist you toward evil and lawlessness?
For he says: "Did you suppose, lawless one, that I too am like you?"
But you, when you seek the friendship of a mortal man, do good to him and always say and do for him whatever you have learned
is pleasing to him; yet for union with God, for becoming his child and attaining to the measure of the Son, you are not eager, but what he hates, that you do.
And by transgressing the law you dishonor him, and through the very thing by which you anger him most, you hope to find forgiveness.
Take care that, through that hope of forgiveness, you do not gather a multitude of evils to yourself, and then have the sin but fail to obtain the forgiveness.
"God is not mocked." Do not make a trade of that grace; do not say that the law is good, but sin is sweet.
Desire is the devil's forge, leading to sin and to destruction; desire is the mother of sin, and sin is the sting of death.
Desire is the nurturer of the eternal worm; it is sweet for a short time to the palate of the one who takes it, but in the end it becomes more bitter than gall, so as to consume him.
This biding of time proclaims nothing other than this: "Let sin reign in me first, and then at some later time let the Lord reign too;
let me present my members to sin as instruments of lawlessness, and then at some later time present them to God as instruments of righteousness."
So too Cain made his offering: he took the first fruits for his own enjoyment and offered the second ones to God, the Creator and Giver.
In the same way you, while you are strong and able to act, spend your youth in sin, and when those instruments of sin have grown feeble,
then you offer them to God, when your body is no longer of any use but only lies prostrate from the failing of your strength.
The chastity of old age is not chastity, but inability to fornicate.
A dead man does not receive a crown. No one is reckoned righteous because of his inability to do evil.
But while you still have the strength, then struggle to keep yourself from sin, for this is virtue:
turning away from evil and doing good; whereas merely being idle from evil deserves neither praise nor punishment.
If you have ceased from sin because of your age, the credit is not yours, but belongs to that weakness.
For we praise those who do good willingly, and not those who are held back from sin by compulsion.
And again, who has set the limit of your life for you? Who has promised you time until old age? Who is so trustworthy a guarantor of things to come?
Do you not see how infants are snatched away by death? How young men pass away? Our life has no single fixed limit.
Why do you wait for baptism to become the gift of a fever [?], when you will not even be able to speak the words of life, and perhaps will not be able to hear them clearly either?
When that sickness has settled in the head, you will not be able to lift your hands to heaven, nor to stand on your feet,
nor to bend your knees in worship, nor to receive instruction properly, nor to confess without error, nor to renounce the enemy,
And perhaps you may not even recognize that great mystery with knowledge, and you may be doubted by those present there, who would say:
"Has he understood the grace, or is he ignorant of these matters?"
And further, even if you receive the grace with knowledge, then you have received the talent but have no opportunity to work at multiplying it.
Be like that eunuch: he found the teacher and did not neglect the teaching.
Instead, the rich man took the poor man up into his chariot, the dignified and wealthy man took up the needy and despised one,
and he learned the gospel of the kingdom and accepted the faith with his heart, and he did not put off receiving the spiritual seal.
For as soon as they came upon water, he said: "Behold, water." This is a word of joy, as if to say: "Behold what we were seeking; what now prevents me from being baptized?"
Where the will is ready, there is no one who hinders, for he who calls is the lover of humankind, the minister is ready, the grace is ungrudging.
Let there be zeal, and let there be no one to ruin it.
There is one who hinders, who blocks the ways of life for us, and let us overcome him through understanding.
He brings this negligence upon us, but let us rise up to fight him.
He deceives our hearts with vain promises, but let us not be ignorant of those schemes of his.
Or is this not always his way of working, who invites us to commit sin today and persuades us to save righteousness for tomorrow?
For this reason the Lord undoes those schemes of his and says: "Today, if you hear my voice."
He says: "Today for me and tomorrow for God." And the Lord cries out: "Today hear my voice."
Understand the wickedness of the enemy: he does not dare to advise that anyone should separate entirely from God, for he knows
that this is grievous for Christians to hear; but by the art of deception he wishes to accomplish his will.
He is wise and full of devices for doing evil; he understands that we humans live in whatever time we are in,
and that every deed is done in the very time in which a person is.
So by stratagem he steals the present day from us and leaves us the hope of tomorrow; and again, when that tomorrow comes,
that wicked companion of ours comes again and says to us: "Let just today be for me and tomorrow for the Lord."
And thus he always wickedly takes from us the day in which we are, leaves us the hope of the one to come, and imperceptibly steals away our life.
I once saw such a contrivance on the part of a bird of many wiles: for its chicks were easy to catch because of their youth,
and for this reason it would throw itself in front of them and, as if ready to be caught, would move about before the hunters.
And it neither allowed them to catch it nor cut off their hope of catching it,
But by such devices it held them with the hope of catching it, and while they were busy with it, it gave the chicks time to flee; and then, last of all, it too went away.
Be afraid that the same thing may happen to you also, when in the hope of uncertain things you abandon what is manifest.
Come, then, and entrust yourself wholly to the Lord; give your name to be enrolled, register with the assembly of the Church, for a soldier is enrolled among soldiers;
an athlete, once he has registered, then enters the contest; a citizen is registered and counted among those of the city.
You share in all of these: as a soldier of Christ, as a contender for the truth, as a citizen of heaven.
Register in this book, so that you may be enrolled in the heavenly one. Learn that good way of life: guarding of the eyes,
restraint of the tongue, subjugation of the flesh, humility of mind, purity of thoughts, doing away with anger.
Whoever commands you, obey him; whoever oppresses you, do not resist him.
Love those who hate you, pray for those who persecute you, bless those who curse you, be dead to sin, be crucified with Christ, turn all your love toward the Lord.
Or are these things difficult? Which of the good things, then, is easy? Who has won a victory by sleeping?
Who has put on the crown of endurance through pleasure and delight? No one has ever been crowned without labor.
Affliction gives birth to glory; labors are what win crowns. I too say that: "Through many afflictions we must enter the kingdom of heaven."
But the blessedness of the kingdom of heaven awaits those afflictions, whereas the bitterness and evil of hell threaten the labors of sin.
For if you investigate well and understand, even the works of the devil are not accomplished without labor by those who practice lawlessness.
For what are the sweats of chastity? Yet the fornicator is forever drenched in sweat, when desire wears him out.
How much could fasting diminish the body in this way, as that evil and defiled lewdness destroys it?
Though those who pray in vigil pass their nights sleepless, those who keep vigil in evil deeds pass them far worse.
For the fear of being exposed, and then again the frenzy toward desire, keep all rest far from him.
But if you flee the narrowness of the way that leads to life and pursue the broad way of sin,
I fear that you may walk the broad way to the end and find also an evil lodging matching your [?] way.
Or is it hard to keep that treasure? But stay awake, brother, and guard it. You can have helpers, if you wish:
prayer as a guard by night, fasting as a helper, psalm-singing as a comforter. Take these with you; let these keep watch with you over the safekeeping of what is precious.
Tell me, then, what is better: that we be rich and then take care to preserve that wealth, or that we have nothing at all that we might guard?
For no one flees from good things for fear of being deprived of them; otherwise, no human undertaking would ever have prospered, if in every matter we did not think of success.
For with farming is found barrenness, with trade shipwreck, with marriage widowhood.
But we begin to do our works in the hope of something better, and the fulfillment of that hope we entrust to our Governor, the Lord.
But you honor holiness in word, while in deed you live among evils.
Take care lest you should at some time repent of those evil designs of yours, when the benefit of repentance no longer exists.
Fear the parable of the virgins, for they had no oil in their vessels, and when they needed to go in with the bridegroom, only then did they realize what they lacked.
For this reason the Word rightly gave them the name of foolish, for they wasted the time when the oil was needed in going here and there and searching for oil, and they did not realize
how they had remained outside and had shut themselves out from the splendor of that bridal chamber.

Therefore take care lest you too put it off from year to year, from day to day, and from hour to hour, and do not receive the oil, the nourishment of the light, and so fall into a day that you did not expect,
when the means of life fail you, and there is distress on every side and unbearable affliction that has no consolation,
when the physicians give you up and your own people give you up, when you are in the grip of that grievous and deadly disease,
when a fierce fever burns your insides and you sigh from the depth of your heart,
but you find no comforter, and you utter some slight and feeble word, and there is no one who would listen, but everything
that you say is regarded as raving, who will give you baptism then? Who will remind you of it, weighed down as you are by the suffering of the disease?
Your own people are distressed and grieving over your death, and they neglect to remind you.
Those who are outside that suffering have no concern for you.
To a friend the reminder is burdensome, as something disturbing; perhaps even the physician deceives you, and you do not give up hope because of the natural love of life.
It is night then, and there is a lack of helpers: either there is no baptizer, or death has arrived, and those who lead you away hurry you on.
Who will be your rescuer then? God, who was always despised by you? Or do you say that he will listen then?
But consider how you listen to him now. Or will he give you time for delay? For the time he has given you, have you used it well?
"Let no one deceive you with vain words." For "destruction will come upon you in an instant," and ruin will come like a whirlwind.
A sorrowful angel will come, who will lead away by force and drag your soul, bound by sins,
which keeps turning back toward this world and lamenting without tears, when the organ of lamentation has been shut.
Oh, how much you will blame yourself then, how much you will sigh uselessly and repent of those evil designs of yours,
when you see the light of the righteous in that splendid distribution of gifts, and the sorrow of sinners in that deep darkness!
Oh, what words will you speak then in the pain of your heart? "Woe is me, why did I not cast off from me this heavy burden of sins,
since it was so easy to cast it off, but through my negligence heaped this burden of these many evils upon my head?
Woe is me! How is it that I did not wash away these defilements of mine, but am instead so stained with sin?
By now I would be with the angels; by now I would be delighting in the good things of heaven. O those wicked counsels!
For the sake of that passing taste of sins I am tormented without end; for the sake of the desires of the flesh I am given over to the fire.
The judgment of God is just: they called me to life and I did not obey; they taught me and I did not listen; they told me what was better, but I laughed."
Words such as these you will speak, and you will weep and mourn for yourself, if you depart before baptism and have gained nothing.
O man, either fear Gehenna, or be full of desire and eagerness for the kingdom. Do not despise the calling by which you have been called.
Do not say, "Let me be excused for this or that reason." No reason at all serves as a true excuse.
I marvel and weep when I recall that you honor shameful deeds more than the great glory of God, and
that for the sake of defiled desire you cannot part from sin, and for this reason you cast yourself out from the good things of the kingdom,
so that you will not see the good things of the heavenly Jerusalem, where there are myriads of angels, assemblies of the firstborn, thrones of the apostles,
dwellings of the prophets, habitations of the patriarchs, crowns of the martyrs, resting places of the righteous.
Desire to number yourself among them, when you are washed and purified by the gift of Christ,
to whom be glory and power, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever, amen.
